title: Stream fingerprinting, per-segment trace correlation, and adaptive redaction orchestration
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Provide deterministic per-segment (aka 'window') metrics and trace correlation for streaming responses while enabling an adaptive redaction orchestration layer that can scrub PII at emit-time without violating latency SLOs. This ticket implements a lightweight fingerprinting header, a span correlation scheme compatible with existing OpenTelemetry traces, and a policy-driven redaction gateway which attaches to the streaming path. The implementation must support sampling, non-deterministic scrub rules, and seamless fallbacks to non-redacted telemetry for high-throughput paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each emitted segment must include a stable stream_fingerprint header and a segment_index metric that appears in Prometheus for both hosted and dedicated modes.

2) Traces for segments must include trace.span_id links to a stream root span so that per-segment latencies and downstream tool-call latencies can be attributed in the Console (A trace search example: stream_fingerprint=<id> should surface all spans).

3) Redaction policies (regex + dictionary + ML classifier tag) can be evaluated inline with per-segment emission and must support three modes: enforce, mask-only, and passthrough. Mode switches are configurable in Console feature flags.

4) End-to-end latency regression < 8ms median added to 95th percentile segment emit path under normal load (no fallback). If classification triggers, documented extra latency budget applies and must be observable.
5) Integration tests that simulate tool-calls interleaved with streaming must preserve span relationships and show no PII in metrics, logs, or traces when enforce mode is active.
6) Dashboard in Console with: per-segment latency histogram, redact-rate over time, sample traces by segment_index, and a canary panel for feature-flagged redaction decisions.
7) Migration guide and rollback plan documented: how to disable fingerprint header and remove redaction gateway without breaking existing dashboards or downstream consumers.
8) Security review completed and signed off by Security team with proof of test vectors and false-positive/negative matrix.
9) Rollout plan with gradual enablement on 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic with automated rollback on SLA breaches.
10) PRs merged and associated Confluence design doc linked in ticket.
11) Updated SDK behavior documented for structured output compatibility layer (notes for Node/Python SDKs).
implementation_notes: Fingerprint: 64-bit truncated SHA256 of (user_id || session_id || stream_start_ts) with base64url encoding. Keep deterministic across retries; regenerate only on explicit stream restart.

Span model: create a stream.root span at request accept; each segment emits a child span stream.segment with attributes: segment.index, segment.tokens, fingerprint. Tool/function-call spans are attached as children of the relevant segment span.

Redaction gateway: run in-path middleware that executes policy engine. For enforce mode, block emits containing high-confidence PII and route to non-streamed fallback with error code + telemetry. Mask-only replaces characters and emits original length metadata.
Sampling strategy: default 5% full-trace sampling, 100% ingest of minimal segment metrics. Configurable via Console per-project flags.
Telemetry sinks: metrics -> metrics ingestion (Prometheus-compatible). Traces -> OpenTelemetry collector. Logs -> redact pipeline before writing to logging backend.
Backpressure: if redaction classifier latency > per-segment budget, automatically fall back to mask-only mode and emit a telemetry event. This behavior is feature-flagged.

Compatibility layer: structured outputs (JSON tool-calls) must be tokenized and included in segment metadata but not emitted as raw traces. Provide an SDK hook to attach structured payload references.
Performance: microbenchmarks indicate adding redaction classifier adds ~3–12ms depending on model; prioritize smaller classifier + rule-based prefilter to avoid tail latency blowups.
Testing: add unit tests for regex rules, e2e harness generating simulated user PII, chaos tests that inject slow classifier responses to verify fallback behavior.
Operational: add SLOs for redact-latency and redact-failure-rate. Add alerting for >1% reject rate or >0.5% fallback-to-passthrough rate over 5m.
Docs: Confluence design should include dataflow diagram, privacy rationale, and SDK migration snippets for Node and Python.

PRs to open: runtime: redaction middleware (repo: infra/runtime-redact), telemetry: add fingerprint and segment metrics (repo: infra/observability), sdk: structured-output reference (repo: client-sdks).
